most_similar_reason: Candidate 9 tells essentially the same myth: the sister-wife goddess whose brother-husband king is murdered by a jealous brother and dismembered, whose scattered pieces she and her sister recover and reassemble, who is magically revived just long enough for her to conceive a son that later avenges him, after which he rules the underworld.
least_similar_reason: Candidate 5 shares nothing with the target beyond generic supernatural agency—it is a shapeshifting rabbit trickster who names animals and slaps a giant lumberjack with a fish, with no murdered king, dismemberment, resurrection, avenging son, or protective mother-goddess.
